content.subject: Sturzflut in Nepal: Viele Tote und über 1300 Vermisste
content.preheader: Das Wichtigste des Tages im Rückblick.

content.title: The most important events of the day in review

content.text: The most important news of the evening: The flood disaster in Nepal and the death of Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic

And you'll only read this in the NZZ: Expectations for the office of the German Federal President are incredibly high. He is supposed to inspire the country and deliver bold, rousing speeches. Finding such a personality is difficult enough – now the successor to the incumbent, Frank-Walter Steinmeier, is also supposed to be a woman for the first time, and on top of that, a bulwark against the right wing. Both requirements are bad ideas. [See commentary]

content.title: Numerous deaths in Nepal flash flood; further floods feared

content.text: What happened: At least 359 people died in the devastating flash flood in the border region between Nepal and China. More than 1,300 are still missing, including eight Germans. Chinese authorities now fear further floods. According to Chinese state television, citing the Ministry of Water Resources, a reservoir formed at a river's mouth on the Nepalese side. There was a risk of a dam breach, sources said. To the latest developments

The background: The flash flood was possibly triggered by a glacier collapse. The fall of the ice masses from a great height could have transformed them into water. However, a glacial lake outburst is also possible. Several glacial lakes in the Himalayas require close monitoring because they are prone to breaching. The flash flood buried entire settlements over a stretch of more than 60 kilometers. For many residents, there was no escape. More on the background

The Gyirong border crossing: The flash flood also destroyed an important border crossing between China and Nepal. It is Beijing's strategic corridor through the Himalayas. A flash flood destroyed the bridge in 2025. Why do Nepal and China nevertheless continue to rely on this dangerous trade route? To the background

content.title: Srebrenica massacre: War criminal Ratko Mladic dead

content.text: What happened: Former Bosnian Serb military leader Ratko Mladic died in The Hague at the age of 84. Mladic was sentenced to life imprisonment for war crimes and served his sentence in the international prison in The Hague. To the report

A look back: Mladic had, among other things, ordered the massacre of more than 8,000 people – mainly men and young men – in the eastern Bosnian enclave of Srebrenica in July 1995. In 2017, he was convicted by the Hague War Crimes Tribunal.
Two dead after violent incident at Brandenburg school: Police arrested a suspect. The background to the crime is still unclear. To the report

Nvidia doubles revenue and profit: With a market capitalization of more than 5 trillion dollars, Nvidia is the world's most valuable listed company. Thanks to the AI boom and the construction of data centers, profits are soaring. Observers, however, warn of a new stock market bubble. To the report

Drug crime escalates in Brussels: Within five days, Brussels authorities registered seven shootings. The Interior Minister speaks of a «national emergency.» The authorities have now announced new measures in the fight against drug crime. To the report

Yayoi Kusama is dead: The Japanese artist died in Tokyo on Aug. 14 at the age of 97, it was announced. Kusama was one of the most important Japanese artists of the post-war period. She became internationally known for her colorful dots, called «Polka Dots.» To the obituary

Yemen in distress: The radical Houthi tribal militia has been killing fighters of the internationally recognized Yemeni government for weeks. After years of wars and crises, the port city of Aden looks dilapidated: only ruins remain of the former luxury hotels, and the plaster is peeling from the whitewashed facades of the houses. The government wants to retake its country. However, the looming armed conflict in Aden is not meeting with great enthusiasm, as a visit shows. To the reportage
With the premium newsletter «NZZ Pro,» you get a look ahead at the global economy and geopolitics. Test it free for 30 days now. Register here

Day of decision: A new state parliament will be elected in Saxony-Anhalt on September 6. Should the AfD gain an absolute majority, this would have far-reaching consequences – for the parties, for Saxony-Anhalt, and for Germany as a whole. What is at stake in the election? To the background

Meta trial: Arturo Béjar is one of the key figures in the wave of lawsuits against the Instagram company Meta. At Facebook, he led the team that dealt with anti-bullying tools and the protection of minors, among other things. He says: «Instagram is a service that invites strangers into our children's bedrooms, at night.» To the interview

Fight against wasps: An ice cream on the beach, a sausage on the balcony – and the black-and-yellow insects are already swarming. We provide tips to get through wasp season unscathed. To the background

🎧 Listen: Millions of vehicles roll over the Brenner Pass in Tyrol every year. The traffic is so burdensome for the narrow valley that resistance is mounting. The «traffic refugees» still come, says Austria correspondent Meret Baumann in «NZZ Akzent.» This even hinders ambulances, she says. To the podcast

📱 Experience: Digital communication technologies have revolutionarily changed the way we interact. What used to be formal and slow is now casual and fast. But who controls the networks and the content? And what does it mean to put an iPad in the hands of toddlers? Join the discussion at the NZZ Podium on September 3 – on site or online. Register here
We wish you a pleasant evening.
Marcel Urech and Kathrin Klette
